If you're a shift leader at that bridge, your duty was to inform the colleagues who were wearing those caps about the reasons why they had to remove their caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I don't understand anything you are telling me. How can a commander give you an order to the effect that you should remove an official symbol from your cap? I understand nothing at all, but let's just leave it at that. And now I may be saying this with my tongue firmly in my cheek when I say I understand nothing. We all know that, but can we please now have a look at a document that was submitted to me by the OTP. This is a public document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no need to keep it secret because it will in no way disclose the identity of this witness. Can it please be placed on our screens? It's the document that I -- that I requested from the OTP. I wanted a translation into English, as well, but they don't seem to have it yet or whatever. I think it should be made public, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This document is not about you personally. It has nothing to do with you, but it pertains to the situation in Bijeljina, and that's why we would like to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have it yet, do we? Can the Registrar please provide copies for the Chamber. There it is. I have it now. I see it on my screen. Let's go through this together. Can we just please get the image to be a bit clearer? This is somewhat blurry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You see the header of this document? May the Registrar please provide a copy for you so that you can look at a hard copy in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If a hard copy can be made available for the witness, the Chamber and the OTP. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You see here, if you look at the header, it reads: "SFRY, Yugoslavia, Federal Minister for All People's Defence," the federal coat of arms of Yugoslavia, and then a text in three scripts languages: Serbian, in both Cyrillic and Latin script; and then Macedonian and Slovenian; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If you look at the signature line: "Chief of the JNA General Staff, Colonel-General Blagoje Adzic." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If you go to the bottom, you see the official Registry number of The Hague Tribunal, 0038-3374. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see who this document is addressed to, Colonel Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, in person. It doesn't say Zeljko. It just says Z. Raznatovic personally; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Pursuant to the law on the armed forces of the SFRY and instructions on service in the armed forces of the SFRY, I hereby order, 1, 2, 3. Can you please be so kind as to read what exactly Blagoje Adzic is ordering Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read it out slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Number 1, start with number 1, and then we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I hereby order: "1. Make a breakthrough along the Bijeljina-Loznica-Visegrad line or axis by driving out the Muslim population, regardless of any casualties. "2. Regardless of any casualties, take hold of all the strategic features. If necessary, involve the units of Jovic, Vucarevic, Nikola Luic, as well as the Herzegovina and Drina Corps and the Uzice Corps. "3. Before the action is launched, link up with Milisav Gagovic and Major-General Ratko Mladic. Continue to operate in concert. The corps and garrison commanders in the areas affected by war operations and mopping-up operations shall be under the command of Colonel Raznatovic and shall be under the obligation of obeying his orders alone and no one else's. If necessary, General Mladic will see to any support that the Tigers, the Wolves from Vucjak, and the White Eagles might need, as well as any support for the air forces. About this, get in touch directly with General Ninkovic or Stevanovic and Bajic."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you please read what the stamp says? It reads: "Federal Secretariat for All People's Defence, Political Administration." Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, sir. You're an experienced police officer. Doesn't it appear to you at first sight that this document is a clumsy example of forgery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you about this document and specifically the orders in it. Not a single one bears a stamp in the upper left corner. Not a single institution is named there in the former Yugoslavia because this is a stamp. This stamp reads: "Political Administration," and frankly, if that's what it says, it should instead read "Federal Secretariat for All People's Defence of the SFRY" or, for example, "All People's Defence Ministry Political Administration," I'm unfamiliar with that. I think this is a case of forgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, there you go. Thank you. Let's try and go through this document together. You provided all of my answers already, but if you look at the header up there, it reads: "Federal Secretary for All People's Defence." You're a police officer. You completed your secondary schooling. You're educated enough to know that the federal secretary was also the defence minister; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A member of the federal government. That's the Defence Ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And yet you know that there's the JNA General Staff, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the General Staff of the JNA is subordinated to the Presidency of the SFRY; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Back in 1987, the JNA General Staff was now made into the General Staff of the armed forces; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it remained under the command of the Presidency of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As an experienced police officer, do you realise that there is no date here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There is no protocol marking here, right, and the rule had to be there, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. So this is a document produced by the general secretary, allegedly. In that case, it should be signed by the federal secretary, Veljko Kadijevic, or the federal minister, right, not Blagoje Adzic; right? Right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If this is a document produced by the General Staff of the armed forces, in that case the header should read: "General Staff," and there should be a stamp there, the General Staff stamp, and not the Political Administration of the Federal Secretary or Federal Secretariat; right? If this had been signed by the Federal Secretariat, there would have been a stamp there of the Federal Secretariat for All People's Defence, the secretary's cabinet; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This political administration is one of the several administrations comprised by the Federal Secretariat; there was Political Administration, Personnel Administration, Security Administration a Quarter-Master's Administration, and so on and so forth; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. So is this such a stupid case of forgery that we're all simply stunned by it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat this: The header in the upper left corner is certainly no original. Any order from the General Staff, Colonel-General Adzic, or the federal secretary can -- no order can read "Federal Secretary." It has to be "Federal Secretariat for All People's Defence," and then if it's in reference to the federal secretary, then it would be "Federal Secretary for All People's Defence." And then lower down it would be "Pursuant to the law on the armed forces of the SFRY," and then the appropriate paragraph, a reference to the appropriate law, what paragraph of that law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the instructions and service, right, the appropriate paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the protocol number under which the order was filed because each order is filed into the protocol book of orders, right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Judges, here is evidence for you of the kind of forgery produced and resorted to by the OTP. This document was served on me several years ago, and it is something that is supposed to be in support of the consolidated indictment against me. Is this sufficient for you to charge the Prosecutor with contempt of court? I don't know. That is up to you to judge. But here is a plain example of the sort of forgery that the OTP are resorting to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I'm seeing this document for the first time of my life, the first time we see this document. It must have been disclosed under the different rules in the regulation that ruled disclosure. Now, if this is a forgery, how is it that the OTP had this document and didn't check into it? Maybe you don't know anything about this document and you're discovering it for the first time, just like me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will determine where we obtained the document from and inform the Trial Chamber accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. Let us move on to the specifics of your written statement and your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, despite the fact that this document might be a forgery, I still note that it would have been the JNA that would have conducted the action against Bijeljina, that Colonel Arkan, whose rank was colonel, obviously, and he was in charge of heading this operation. Furthermore, General Mladic could, if need be, provide support to the Tigers, the White Eagles, the Grey Wolves, and I note that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party are also mentioned as well as other volunteers. This is what the document is all about. Now, it's up to the Prosecution to find how it came up with this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... this, Mr. President. Where have you found volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party? They're not mentioned anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said this. There must have been a problem in the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the translation I received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg the interpreters, once again, be very careful with your interpretation. I said that in this document there is mention of the possible role played by General Mladic in case of providing, if need be, support to the following units: The Wolves, the Tigers and the White Eagles. And I added that I noted that in this paragraph, there is no mention of the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is absolutely a forgery, an ill-intentioned and definite forgery, and this forgery has been produced by The Hague OTP. Such a document is quite impossible in the practice of the activities of the Federal Secretariat for National Defence and the Chief of Staff of the armed forces. This is a nonexistent document. This is something manufactured by The Hague Prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Don't say that it's the OTP which fabricated this document. This is a very serious accusation. The Prosecution must have received this document from someone, from a witness, from the Serbian authorities. I have no idea who sent this document in the first place, and when he received the document, it was disclosed to you. Otherwise, you know, you are -- this would be very serious. This is a very serious allegation, you know, that an international tribunal would be fabricating documents. This is a very serious accusation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As if that would be the first time, Mr. President, as if there aren't many other cases when they produce false documents, even false indictments.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as with much of what the accused alleges, this really doesn't merit much of a response. I will indicate, however, that this document was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't agree with you. I don't agree with you. I don't think that you can say this merits no answer. There is a document. It was disclosed to him officially through the official channel, and he's saying this is -- he's saying that this is a forgery. We can't just, like, set it aside. I believe that the OTP must absolutely look into the origin of this document, see who provided this document to you, whether you were instrumented -- you were manipulated by the person who actually gave you this document. This must be dealt with with the utmost seriousness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the allegations that the accused continues to make about fabricating documents, fabricating evidence, false indictments, is not something that we are prepared to deal with each and every time he raises it because, quite frankly, he's doing it for political reasons outside of this courtroom, and it is not, in our respectful view, a proper use of the limited time we have available to us. This document was provided to the Prosecution by a Defence counsel in another case. It was simply disclosed to the accused. We have not tendered this document. We have not sought to rely on this document. The accused has simply presented a document that was disclosed to him, flagged it up as some kind of Prosecution-fabricated document. It is a complete waste of everyone's time for us to continue talking about this. When we identify documents that may contain Rule 68 material, it's disclosed to the accused. That does not mean in any way, shape, or form that the OTP adopts the document. We disclose material that we believe, on its face, contains information that the accused might think is exculpatory. If he chooses to use it and it helps his case, fine. If he brings in documents and simply makes allegations that OTP -- unfounded allegations that OTP has created a document, that is improper. The document was provided to us, as I've indicated, by Defence counsel in another case, and it was disclosed to the accused because our searches indicated that it might contain material that was exculpatory due to the search terms used that presumably included the name of Mr. Arkan. But we're not going to go into the merits of whether this is a fabricated document or not. This is simply a waste of our time, in our respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This document was handed to the OTP by counsel of Defence, but we don't know which counsel of Defence, we don't know who it is, and then the OTP disclosed it to the accused under Rule 68. Very well. So as long as you're handed a document, you disclose it. That's the conclusion I draw from this. Proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it seems to be that I am again to blame because of this forgery. It is the duty of the Prosecutor to tell us from which Defence counsel and in which case he received this. The Defence counsel cannot be relieved of responsibility. We must know the name of that person and the case. What kind of a person would I be if I had even tried to use this document as exculpatory material? As the Prosecutor said, this was disclosed to me under Rule 68(1). Is this kind -- is this intended to mislead, to compromise my entire defence? Imagine if I was stupid enough or as stupid as the Prosecution thought I was to in haste use this document as exculpatory in my defence, and then my whole defence would break into pieces on that basis. This is not such a minor issue, and I insist, Mr. President, that the Prosecutor tells us from whom -- from which lawyer he deceived [as interpreted] this document as an exculpatory one, and that lawyer must be suspended and prohibited from appearing before an international court, even before a national court. Do we need to conceal the identity of that attorney now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Trial Chamber has been seized by this oral submission of yours and will deliberate on this. Proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1035, in paragraph 8, and you also said in the examination-in-chief, that at the beginning of 1992, you had problems in executing your duties. You're a traffic policeman. And then you say: "If I was to approach a Serb or a reserve officer of the JNA with the intention of fining him for a traffic offence, they would make it clear to me that I could do nothing to them because I was a Muslim and they were a Serb. Does that mean that all the Serbs in Bijeljina knew you and that they knew you were a Muslim, but when stopping anyone in traffic and trying to fine them, you don't tell anyone your name? "A. No, I have been stopped hundreds of times by traffic policemen, and no one ever introduced himself, nor did I ask them to introduce themselves." And then you say that you had problems with the reserve officers of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You should know that as a policeman, you are not competent for JNA officers in uniform, whether they're active duty or reservists. The moment he puts on a uniform, then it is only the military police that has competencies over him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if he's moving in a military vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you have no right to detain a JNA officer if he shows you his official ID, whether he's a reserve or active duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he commits an offence, I can detain him or I can inform the military police. We're talking about a traffic offence. In that case, not a single officer is exempted from paying a fine for an offence he may have made, and he's not exempt from my control if he's moving in a private civilian vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But not a single officer is relieved of responsibility for a traffic offence, yes, but the procedure is different. You stop a reserve officer and you tell him, You have been speeding, driving at such and such a speed, the fine is such and such; and wearing a uniform, he shows you his official ID confirming that he's a JNA officer, and your only possible measure is to report to the military police, for them to take over the case.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, surely you didn't have the right to arrest him. You had no right to detain and arrest him. You never had that right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us clear this up. One thing is to ask for his ID, and to detain him is another. If he refuses to pay the fine for the offence he has made, then I file a report, and that report is not filed with the military police, the military organ, but to the magistrates courts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, if he refuses to pay a fine, that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There might be a mistake on page 60, line 24. My fellow Judge has signaled this to me. Mr. Seselj is putting a question to you. You're a police officer, you're in charge of traffic, and therefore, you are competent when it comes to traffic offences, and then he looks into this, and in English on line 24, you answer, saying: "No." In French, it was a "Yes." So it seems that we have a problem here. Let me put the question again to the witness. When a JNA officer is in a military vehicle, are you entitled to control this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A JNA officer driving a military vehicle, then I have -- the civilian police has no right to control him. But if he's driving in a civilian vehicle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. I'll go step by step. The second question now. Let's imagine we have a JNA officer in full uniform in a private car, let's say in a Golf, for example, registered in Germany, for example. Are you entitled to check this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An officer driving a car with foreign registration plates, for instance, for Germany, something he was not allowed to do; but if he's driving a vehicle with civilian registration plates or German or French registration plates, you can stop him and control him if there is an offence made. You ask him to pay the fine on the spot, or you can write a report to the magistrates court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let me make this a bit more complex. Let's say it's a JNA officer in a private car, but let's say that he tells you that this vehicle has been requisitioned by the army. Are you entitled, then, to check and control him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to see his documents. For the requisitioning of that vehicle, he must have a written certificate showing that that vehicle has been requisitioned by the JNA. This document does not relate to him but to the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let me now refer to something that surprised me most. You made a statement in 1997 and in 2001. In neither of those statements do you mention my name or the Serbian Radical Party or Mirko Blagojevic, and now suddenly, just before your appearance in court, on the 8th -- no, on the 2nd of September, 2008, you now speak of Mirko Blagojevic. In paragraph 26, you say all the police personnel in Bijeljina knew Mirko Blagojevic and his brother as criminals long before the conflict; Mirko Blagojevic was a member of the SDS, of the Serbian Democratic Party in Bijeljina, and one of Seselj's men. Please, was Mirko Blagojevic ever had -- did he ever have a criminal record? As a policeman in Bijeljina, you should know that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of Yugoslavia, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see. He was never punished on the territory of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I believe, what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How could you say, then, that he was a criminal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information of the Crime Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What did the Crime Service know about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much more than I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What, specifically? Tell me so that I should know. I hear of that for the first time. I'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, he engaged in criminal activities abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abroad. I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was it in Zambia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In Europe. Was it in Spain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with precision. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What kind of criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stealing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What, stealing what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're a serious person. You're a professional policeman with some experience. If you say of a living man who until recently was a deputy in the Joint Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, who is to this day a deputy in the Municipal Assembly of Bijeljina, who is President of the Party of Serb Radicals, which contains my name in its name in the Republika Srpska, when you say of him that he's a criminal in such an important official document, and I think you repeated that in the courtroom, surely you have to have some evidence of that. Just imagine if I were to say of you that you were a criminal. I have no evidence. I never heard of any particular crime that you may have committed. I have no evidence that you committed a war crime. Just imagine if I were to say of you that you were a criminal. Wouldn't that be terrible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to defend myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why would you have to defend yourself if I have no evidence? Why should Mirko Blagojevic defend himself, or why should I defend him, if you don't have a single piece of specific evidence to prove that he was ever a criminal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally don't have any evidence. All I can say, that the Crime Service, even before this party was founded, that is, before all the parties were founded, that there was some analysis of persons such as Mirko Blagojevic and others. And I can say, among other things, that I learnt from my colleagues who worked in that service about meetings that were held at those parties and what he did before, but I personally don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But what was he? He was simply registered as a Serb nationalist, that's all, and nothing more than that. He was never charged with anything before any court. He was never charged with a single crime. And what is this like? You pin crimes on to someone. You label him as a criminal with no reason at all. He is the chief Radical in Republika Srpska. If he's a criminal, then I'm a criminal too. He enjoys my complete trust. He's a long-time friend. We go way back, before the Serb Radical Party was ever established. You know that I used to go to Bijeljina before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know when I visited?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that I was there some months before the armed clashes broke out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is I did not personally see you there, Mr. Seselj. But each time you visited, this is something that would be known.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The police would know about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they would provide -- they would monitor my movements around Bijeljina whenever I was there, discreetly, but every step I made; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let me be straight and open about this. Those were other services that were involved in that type of work, and I can't say I monitored you myself. I simply don't know. But every time you visited, the police knew about it. The police knew you were in Cafe Srbija with Mirko Blagojevic, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That could hardly have been keep secret; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was being monitored.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Everybody knew that I was a major Serb nationalist, the biggest Serb nationalist, perhaps, the most fervent. Do you know of anyone who is a more fervent Serb nationalist than I am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, frankly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There you go. That's one thing that we agree on entirely. For example, six months before the conflict, were you aware of my visits to Bijeljina? Did I make any visits to Bijeljina as far as you could tell? Let's assume the clashes broke out on the last day of March 1992. Did I visit Bijeljina at any point during the latter half of 1992 or the first three months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know any differently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I don't know that, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm asking you because we had a witness here whose evidence I challenged, who said that just before the clashes broke out, I had visited Bijeljina. If I'd been there, you would have known about it; right? The word would have gone 'round, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. Let's move on to a different issue now. In the previous paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, before we leave paragraph 26, I would like to put a question to the witness in respect of the next sentence of that paragraph because, Mr. Witness, you seem to have told the investigator from the Prosecution that Mr. Mirko Blagojevic was a member of the SDS, and yet in the video-clip we heard yesterday, Mr. Blagojevic himself introduced him as the leader of the SRS volunteers. So my question to you is: Where does this membership of the SDS come from? Did you tell the investigator that he was a member of the SDS, and where did you know this from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may have been a misinterpretation. He was not a member of the SDS, not as far as I knew. I know that he was with the Radicals. That's all I know. But the SDS, that was probably a typo, an error. The Serb Radical Party, SRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So you are entering a correction to the statement in paragraph 26; is that correctly understood, that you meant to say that Mr. Blagojevic was a member of the SRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm trying to find some things about your credibility. You have made a statement in 1997. I have this statement, and nowhere in this statement is there any mention of Mr. Seselj or of the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. However, in this statement, you really stress the role played by Arkan. When you testified in 1997, did the OTP tell you which case you were going to testify in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I gave a statement, this main statement that I gave the first time around. Its scope is far broader than the one that I think you have, and my statement in its entirety, if you look at it, shows you the overall goings-on in 1991 and 1992. It was about several different procedures that were in progress.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all the other microphones in the courtroom please be switched off. We cannot hear the witness at all on account of the enormous background noise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For example, no mention was made of Mr. Seselj or anyone else in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. You say that you made an initial statement that was a lengthy one. In what year did you make that statement? Because we have three statements, the one dating back to 1997, the one dating to 2001, and the 2008 statement. So the lengthy statement that you just referred to, when did that take place? Was it done here with the OTP, or was it done before other investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, I gave a statement to Germany's crime police, and then I provided the exact date and year. I can't say really, but that was the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpretation will proceed as soon as all of the sources of background noise have been eliminated and we can hear the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Germany, to what investigators did you make a statement? Were they German investigators? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The German investigators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were all German, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they were Germans. They were working for Germany's crime police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And so they asked you questions in the German language because you speak German? They asked you questions in German, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, in Bosnian, Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your own language. Well, when you met with the investigators from OTP, they said to you that you were going to be testifying in the Milosevic or the Seselj case or in both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was told that it depended on what was necessary as the proceedings progressed. I would be called as a witness. If there is something in my statement about the Milosevic trial, it would be the Milosevic trial. If there was something about the Seselj trial, I would be called to testify in that trial. But it wasn't specified at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were not told in which case they would be using your statements? They didn't say, You'll come to the Milosevic trial, or to Seselj's trial, or anybody else's trial; nobody said to you at any time in which case you would be testifying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but very soon there was another visit by The Hague investigators in relation to whichever trial was going on at the time. For example, they wanted another statement that was in relation to one of the ongoing procedures at the time, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you testified in the Milosevic trial, at any time were you asked questions about the volunteers from the Serb Radical Party; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Perhaps now you will remember the last statement that you made, which is a recent one. It dates back to the 2nd of September, 2008, just a few months ago. Now, that statement has been taken down. How did that happen? Were you told to tell the whole story, or did they ask you very specific questions and you answered those questions? You were a policeman, and of course you understand what I'm driving at. Were they the ones who said to you to narrate all the events and then they summarised them in the document, or else did they ask you questions about specific topics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After my first statement, something was said about the preparations for the Seselj case, what was relevant --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not answering my question. On the 2nd of September, 2008, you met with two investigators, one of whom is here - I won't give you his name - one interpreter, as well, and they heard you for the purpose of having your statement under Article 92 ter, and they said to you, Sir, could you tell us from the start the whole story, what you saw, heard, et cetera; or else, did they say, We shall deal with separate topics; the first topic, yourself and your professional background, and they then asked you to talk about yourself; and then as to your background and personality, they drafted three paragraphs? I just want to know how this was done. There's no trap in my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I can say is to repeat something that I said already. The statement that I provided --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There is background noise. We can't hear the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and then I was asked questions about my previous statement and as far as it was relevant to this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. Now, as of paragraph 16, they call this mopping up in Bijeljina, picking up of corpses in Bijeljina. So as of paragraph 16, you start talking about the 48 bodies, et cetera, and then all of a sudden we see paragraph 22 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 26, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, we talk about bodies being collected, and then we talk about Mirko Blagojevic, and here what you say is the whole police station in Bijeljina knew Mirko Blagojevic and his brother as being criminals. Mirko Blagojevic was a member of the SDS in Bijeljina and one of Seselj's men. So are you the one who spontaneously came forward with this information or did the investigators say, Do you know Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, based on my previous statement, and I think I -- [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And you are the one who said that Blagojevic was a member or was one of Seselj's men, rather?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. A member of Seselj's party. We can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a member of Seselj's party. He was a member at that time or became a member later on? There's a difference. Was he a member in 1992, in the month of May 1992, or was -- did he become a member later on, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I can't answer that one. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Last question, because earlier on Mr. Seselj asked you a series of questions and you answered, but it wasn't very clear. It seemed to me that at some time you were deputy, so I understood that you were elected at the Municipality of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mirko Blagojevic, Mr. President. There might have been the misinterpretation. Mirko Blagojevic was a deputy in Bosnia and Herzegovina, a federal one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good. Very good. And when Mirko Blagojevic, who was an MP in Bosnia-Herzegovina, when -- he was elected on a list of the Serbian Radical Party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the Serb Radical Party, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were the elections following the Dayton Accords. That was after 2000, I think, when he was a deputy to the Joint Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Before that, he was a deputy to the National Assembly of Republika Srpska, two terms of office consecutive, I think. But that's hardly of any consequence now. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. VS-1035, in your first statement, dated the 3rd of June, 1997, in your second statement dated the 22nd of October, 2001, and in the entire transcript of your evidence in the Milosevic trial, and your appearance - there was quite a lengthy one, right - there is not a single reference to my name, to the name of Mirko Blagojevic, or the Serb Radical Party, not a single one. Yet now you appear in September before Mr. Mussemeyer, and he tells you you're supposed to testify in the Seselj case. Was that the first time you heard that you would be appearing in this case, in September last year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When was the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A long, long time ago, I was told by The Hague investigators that, should the need arise and if they believed there was anything in my statement that might be relevant to the case or to any other case, the Krajisnik case, the Plavsic, the Milosevic case, your case, that my evidence would be used and that if necessary I would be called.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2001, when I gave my second statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. VS-1035, in 2001 no one had any idea that there would be an indictment against me to begin with, least of all the OTP. Don't protect the OTP. There's no need for that. You certainly weren't told that at the time, not by them; is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Quite right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can confirm that I was told this in relation to all of the accused who were here, if needed, for the purposes of the Defence, the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But my name was not mentioned, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. You're saying what The Hague Prosecution is saying. You're defending it, and they're not defending it themselves. They say, addressing the Trial Chamber, since the Trial Chamber allowed them to request again that your statement be taken as 92 ter - there's no need for me to elaborate on that - and it says in accordance with that, the OTP has reviewed the body of evidence linked to this witness - therefore, that is the evidence used by Mr. Mussemeyer in the examination-in-chief and probably the Prosecutor in the Milosevic case - and prepared a revised version of the witness statement relating specifically to this case: "Having reviewed the statement in his own language, the witness signed it on the 2nd of September, 2008." So the Prosecution admits that it prepared this statement of yours, this third statement, and then you reviewed that statement and signed it; is that how it went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, how did it go, then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Prosecution came, and one day we worked on my first statement, and then this statement was prepared that was signed in September. It wasn't prepared beforehand. Each of my statements was reviewed again with respect to the topics relevant to this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. You're now defending the Prosecution, but the Prosecution says that they prepared the revised version, which means that the Prosecution had in mind everything else you had signed earlier on in your previous statements, your testimony in the Milosevic case, and on that basis they prepared a lengthier statement. But this OTP would not be true to itself had it not thought of adding something that you had no idea about earlier on, to add the statement that Mirko Blagojevic was known as a criminal, that he was a member of the Serbian Democratic Party. You didn't even notice this when you signed it. Surely, you would have corrected it. He never was a member of the Serbian Democratic Party. But what's the most important thing: In your first statement, you say that a father and his two sons, Muslims, were killed on the pavement in front of their house, 300 metres from the hospital, and you also said that one of the sons was killed -- shot in the forehead at close range. And now, in this latest statement, paragraph 25, following instructions from the OTP, you add: "My relatives told me ..." so there's an intermediary, "... that the wife of the man and the mother of two sons had said that the murder had been done by Damo [as interpreted], known as Sumar, a member of the Blagojevic's men." So this is hearsay. You're making accusations against Branislav Filipovic, called Sumar, who is dead now, that he killed these people. You know how the fighting went on in Bijeljina. You showed us on the map where this Srbija Cafe is, didn't you? The hospital is quite a long way away. It's quite a long way away, and it is not in the part of the centre of Bijeljina where Blagojevic's men were fighting. They were fighting in the surroundings of the Srbija Cafe, the municipality building, and the bus station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I cannot confirm this. I don't know. I didn't see this. You know much more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How come that now, after so many years, surely it would have been quite logical if you knew that Branislav Filipovic, known as Sumar, had killed these three men - that's a terrible crime - that you should have said that immediately in 1997 when it was still fresh in your mind, and to say this in the Milosevic case and not now in the case against me? And let me add to this question. The OTP knows that I refused to examine witnesses under 92 ter, and the Prosecution knows if they add this to your statement and the Trial Chamber admits it, that the statement goes into the file, it goes without any response on my part. Are you claiming today that Branislav Filipovic, known as Sumar, killed these three people, the father and two sons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Answer the question, and then I'll give you the floor. Mr. Seselj is asking you a very clear question, Witness. Can you answer this, and then I will give the floor to Mr. Mussemeyer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not true that I said this subsequently. My first statement about the murder of these three people, who were in the JNA street, figured from in my very first statement, and it was linked to Mr. Branislav, Sumar, because I received that same information from the wife of the killed person, that is, the father and the mother of those two men, and I had to explain that to the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But where is that in your statement? On page 5 in your first statement, in the middle of the paragraph, you say that you remember a father and two sons who were shot on the pavement in front of their house, which was 300 metres behind the hospital in the JNA street. One son was shot in the forehead at close range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Prosecutor is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... interrupting me when it's most interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I didn't interrupt you while you were speaking [indiscernible] to you. But what I want -- it may be that I'm not in the position to clarify this in the position as a Prosecutor. I was a witness when this statement was taken. I only want to clarify that every -- we drafted the statement from the first statement and the second statement the witness has given and from his testimony, and every time, we put the source of it at the end of the paragraph. You can see this. This draft was translated into B/C/S. We brought it to the witness. The witness read it, and he made his annotations and corrections all the time, and where you can see no quote, this is what the witness told us at the end, and it was added according to the witness. He remembered certain things and added this, and we had no quote from former statements, just to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the Prosecutor had no right to provide this clarification. Who can take the Prosecutor at his word? No court can without question take the word of the Prosecutor. If there are proceedings against Mr. Mussemeyer, then he can go into explanations. It is up to me to state what is happening here on the basis of the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And I repeat, you never said earlier on that Branislav Filipovic, known as Sumar, killed these three men. You didn't say that in the Milosevic case. I have the complete transcripts from that case, nor did you say this in your first two statements. It was only when the Prosecutor was preparing you for testimony in this trial this has been added to the text. Who suggested that you make this addition, if you made that addition yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must repeat. My first statement was linked to the killing of these three men. I said that then. Now, whether you have it before you or not, I don't know. Whether I had that during the Milosevic case, I can't remember whether there was a specific question by the Prosecution or the Judges about this, who killed those three men, but I know that my first statement referred to information that I had that this related to Mr. Branislav, Sumar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But it's not there. The Trial Chamber has your first statement. The Prosecutor has your first statement. It is page 5, central paragraph. It is not to be found in the entire transcript of the Milosevic case. It's not there. Very well. It's not there. What can we do about it? Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, that first statement, well, it would seem that that was the one you made with the German police, and we don't have that statement. In the first statement dating back to 1997 that everybody does have here, well, the question of Branislav Filipovic is not mentioned. So the first statement is the one that was made before the German police, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And where is that statement, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody has this. Indeed, nobody has that. The OTP, have you ever had this statement made to the German police, or are you learning about it today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I am not sure, but I think it's the first time I hear about it. I'm not aware and I never saw this statement. I'm only aware of the OTP statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, did you inform the OTP or the Tribunal's investigator of the fact that you had previously made a statement -- previous to 1997 made a statement to investigators from Germany, in Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At our first meeting, it was on the basis of that meeting that I had my first encounter with the investigators of this Tribunal, and they were familiar -- they knew that I had given that statement already. Now, whether they received it or not, or whether it was prompted by this that they took another statement from me, I don't know. This relates to the police in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was checking the transcript from the witness testimony in Milosevic, and in fact he is mentioning Sumar. It's on page 18644, where he was shown a picture, a photo, and he says: "As far as I'm able to recognise him, I think it is Sumar. "Q. And this person by the name Sumar, what information are you able to provide about Sumar with respect to his involvement in Bijeljina? "A. As far as I know, he was a member of the White Eagles, and most of the people killed, as far as I was able to learn, were killed by his group, especially the person killed in the JNA street. "Q. Did you speak to the wife of one of the victims whose body you recovered in Bijeljina? "A. Yes, the mother of the three persons I found in the JNA street next to the library told me that Brano, Sumar, himself had come, taken the three people out of the house and killed them in the street in front of the house." So far the quote from the Milosevic transcript. So he mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a reference to the White Eagles. You see that the witness is talking second-hand or third-hand. He's identifying the White Eagles group, and he refers to them in other places, and about whose existence there are official documents, that the White Eagles did this, and he attaches Sumar to the White Eagles, and now he's attaching Sumar to Mirko Blagojevic. Surely, this is something you should have cleared up with him. Why did he say "White Eagles" earlier on? Branislav Filipovic, Sumar, could not have physically been in that spot. If you look at the improvised map, you will see where the hospital is and where the Srbija Cafe is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What you've just said is on the transcript. We'll now break for 20 minutes, and, Mr. Seselj, you will have 40 minutes left. We'll finish this hearing with this witness. This means that we will not be able to hear the other witness. It seems obvious now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to my information, the conflict in Bijeljina started on the 31st of March, and it continued on the 1st and 2nd of April, and on the 3rd of April it was over by the defeat of the Muslim forces. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know how the conflict started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, it started when a bomb was thrown into the Istanbul Cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who threw that bomb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the person was never identified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So a bomb was thrown, the police carried out an inquiry, some minor material damage was done, and the perpetrator was never found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was not identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And this was before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the building of barricades started that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I think you're confusing things. Let me remind you. Do you know who Alija Gusalic is? He's well known in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you agree that he is a person of very poor moral qualities, without any job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know him personally, but I know that he took part in these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're not aware of his criminal past?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he went to a special school for retarded children, elementary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that on the 31st of March, in the afternoon/early evening, he got on a horse, and in front of the Istanbul Cafe, with a bomb in his hand, galloped past towards the Srbija Cafe, intending to throw the bomb at the Srbija Cafe? The whole of Bijeljina knows this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in front of the Srbija Cafe, there were Serbs standing. It was spring-time, quite warm. There were people standing in front of the cafe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when Mirko Blagojevic saw him galloping on his horse with a bomb in his hand, he fired his pistol and hit him in the leg; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but I can't confirm this. I wasn't in Bijeljina just then. It's possible that that is how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Alija Gusalic didn't manage to throw that hand-grenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I heard. He was hit before he opened the fuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I wasn't there, either. I heard this from other people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that is when the shooting started. According to my information, the Muslims put up 24 barricades in the centre of Bijeljina; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I was told this by eye-witnesses and the participants, and they had control over the whole centre of Bijeljina; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the centre of Bijeljina, only people under Mirko Blagojevic's control were there, and they were the first to respond and to take part in the conflict. Do you know that Mirko Blagojevic and his men were members of the TO, were part of the TO at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he outside the regular TO forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was outside the regular TO forces because before that, his men, armed men, provided security of the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That is one thing, but to take part in armed conflicts is another. This was not the reason; it was the trigger. If that had not triggered it, something else would have because passions and tensions were running high; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just saying that I can't remember whether the grenade was thrown into the Istanbul Cafe first or was this Alija Gusalic who was galloping towards the other cafe first, which of the two events took place first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I know the grenade was thrown at the Istanbul Cafe, that came first, but there was no shooting after that. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- actually, I am not sure about the date, but I think what triggered the events was the grenade in the Istanbul Cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the grenade was thrown into the Istanbul Cafe, no one was hurt; isn't that so? The police came to carry out an investigation, so the police were still operational in the whole town; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A colleague who was a member of the SUP was injured by that grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He happened to be there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had the good fortune that this was a grenade with small balls in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's an offensive or a defensive weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the offensive one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us say it's the black one. This is an offensive grenade because you throw this grenade. If you throw the defensive type, then it can hurt you, too, but the offensive one cannot, and what was that policeman by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Muslim. He was not a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, why did you say he was a colleague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he worked in the Secretariat of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was he involved in the throwing of that grenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe it. He was a guest. I must say he is an employee of the SUP, but I think he was working in the Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. In your previous statement, you talked about the existence of the JNA reservists - that was a JNA unit, right - the TO, the Serb National Guard, and the Serb Volunteers Guard. You never mentioned Blagojevic's men as an independent unit, never, ever, so the Serb Volunteer's Guard at the people who came with Arkan's men; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know how many men in total Arkan brought to the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you. A total of 30?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Probably. Not many, right? Okay. The Serb National Guard was established by Mauzer; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Mauzer was close with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. They were together from the outbreak of these clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From the very outset. Okay. Do you know that they remained close over the following years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Is it true when on the 3rd of April when the Muslims were defeated, most of those involved in the clashes managed to leave Bijeljina, right, and left for Brcko, as far as I know, or someplace else? I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true that the Muslims who remained in Bijeljina surrendered to the Serb forces? I'm saying the Serb forces. The Muslims forces, although in the Serb forces there were a great many Muslims, actually, quite a considerable number of them; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay. I'll convince you later on. Is it true that the Muslims, once the clashes had ended, surrendered to the Serb forces about 500 long barrels? When I say "long barrels," I mean rifles, semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, carbine rifles, that sort of thing. Is this something that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number of pieces that were handed over. Most of the weapons were small arms or pistols, some hunting rifles, maybe a handful of automatic rifles, but I wasn't aware of a huge amount of automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I didn't say a huge amount of automatic weapons. I said about 500 long barrels. Did you see the actual heap when the weapons were surrendered and piled up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the weapons were surrendered at the SUP station, and the figures don't seem to tally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Maybe somebody simply stole part of it before it ever got to the SUP building. This was sometimes the case, somebody took a shine to a certain rifle and then they just nick it; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you say that a total of 48 people were killed during the clashes in Bijeljina. Based on what I know, the clashes went on for those four days, and a total of 38 people were killed, 22 of them Muslims, 15 Serbs, and a Croat lady. Ten people were killed over the following month in the aftermath when various groups were marauding the Bijeljina area; that's what the MUP chief is telling us about; you read that document, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I say was about the bodies that I collected, and that's in the sketch that we looked at. Those are bodies that I personally took to the morgue at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your count was 48?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the hospital, the body count was 48. It's not the number of bodies that I brought there. The number I'm telling you about is the number of people that I brought there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true that the Muslim forces at the beginning of the clashes already had a machine-gun that was mounted at the so-called water-tower? You know the water-tower. You probably know about that more than I do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm familiar with that. I don't believe that. A machine-gun would be impossible to mount there because it would be very difficult to target anything from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why would it be difficult?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to operate a machine-gun like that, you must have a surface on which you can mount it. As far as I know, by looking at the water-tower, there's a window, and opening it up there, it would have been very difficult to handle a machine-gun there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why would one not be able to mount a machine-gun on a window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small one like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A machine-gun, as an infantry weapon, is standard issue; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an automatic rifle, but a machine-gun is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's an automatic rifle. We refer to it often as a machine-gun, but it wasn't a heavy machine-gun; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know that the Muslims had a number of sharp-shooters or snipers deployed around the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say. I don't know that there were any sniper nests at all. Don't get me wrong. I can't say because I didn't see, nor did I hear of anyone being there and sniping from those positions. What I can tell you is that there were pockets of resistance by the Muslim population. There certainly were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you know that the Muslims had a bunker in the park which is in the town centre, a makeshift bunker?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't. All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. You told us about the executions of Muslim civilians. I'm not challenging that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let's be clear about this. This could be quite surprising and incredible. Mr. Seselj is asking you whether the Muslims had a bunker in the city centre. I mean, a bunker is quite obvious. You say, "No." I don't know where he got his information. Are you absolutely sure that there was no bunker in the city centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The park in Bijeljina's town centre is not that large, really. You would see a bunker. I don't think you could build a bunker in a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. You spoke about several Muslim civilians who were killed. They were shot on the spot where they were found. Nevertheless, I have to tell you that this happened to a number of Serb civilians too. Is that something you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. It's true. Some bits of information for you. Do you know about Galac Street; where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Galac? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to my information, the Muslim forces shot the 19-year-old Zvonko Lazarevic there. Have you heard of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You haven't. All right. Do you know that Zvonko Lazarevic was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you know that Antonija Ostojic was killed? She was born in 1926.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I don't know. I'm not privy to these names, but I can tell you about that sketch and my evidence about that sketch. There is a rough location given for Serb victims --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's just try to move things along a little bit and hurry things along a little. I will give some information to you, and you confirm or deny whether you know anything about that. Do you know that a Serb named Risto Stevanovic was killed in much the same way, and this person was not at all involved in the fighting? If you don't know, I just move on; that simple.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what about a Serb who was killed while riding a bicycle by a sniper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who killed him, but I know that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know about a Serb who was mentally retarded who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You did. Okay. We won't mention his name. There would be no point to it. Do you know that the Muslim forces killed a Croatian lady named Marija Ilic at her door-step? Her son Tomislav witnessed the killing of Marija Ilic by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the lady was probably killed, the Croat lady, because there is information to that effect in my statement about a Croat lady being among the casualties. I can't say who killed her because I don't know. I have no information indicating who it was who killed her. You probably know better than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Then what about the mosque in the town centre, one of the mosques in the town centre, that there was a machine-gun nest on top of the mosque; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, based on the information we received when we came to the station, there was something in the town centre, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On top of the mosque; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that Coso Nargalic was the commander of the Muslim barricades; have you ever heard that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with the name, but I don't know about him being in command of the barricades. I can't confirm that, but I don't believe that that was, in fact, the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what about Hasan Dusic? Does that ring a bell? Apparently, he led the attack on the Serbs. He was the founder of a unit that after he was killed was named the Black Swans. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The unit rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At first it was a paramilitary unit, and then later it became part of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, let's see the other side of this coin. Do you know about Gvozdevici? It's a village; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know there were clashes that broke out among the Muslims there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that, and I have family there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yet you don't know about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never learned about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that a substantial number of Muslims were involved in the fighting on the side of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after June and July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, no, no, during the clashes in April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I knew of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You didn't. All right. And what about Sergeant Admir Smajic, a Muslim, a person who was killed while fighting the Muslims in those first days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When was he killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was killed in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a member of the JNA. He was a member of the JNA. I think he was killed in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Aren't you confusing him with somebody else? According to my information, he was killed while fighting the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
