utterances.text: No. I think he was a regular officer of the army, and he was killed somewhere in Croatia, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please, please, I verified some of this information. Maybe this is not all impeccable or perfectly accurate, but that's why I'm asking you. Tell me what you know. That's how it works. Do you know that by a decision of the Serb authorities, a street in Bijeljina was named after him, Admir Smajic Street, which used to be called the Jaksic Brothers Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine. Fine. What about Ibrahim Belgic [phoen] and Asim Vidahic [phoen]? They, too, were killed in the fighting around the Bijeljina city park; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the names. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You told us about the fact that later on, more Muslims were fighting with the Serb forces, had joined the Serb forces. I looked at the BH media and press a little bit, and last year I came across a very interesting feature entitled: "Muslims with cockades." We don't have that much time, so I won't be showing it to you, but do you see how beautiful it is to see a Serb cockade on a Muslim fez cap. Doesn't it look nice? I find it looks lovely. I think the Muslims are actually our brethren. They're just Serbs who happen to be Muslim too. You see how nice it looks, this cockade on the Muslim fez cap. The 3rd Semberija Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska was established, 95 per cent of its composition were Muslims; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a unit like that, and as far as I know, the same unit or part of its command were captured by --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Croats; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the Croats or the BH Army somewhere around Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was this not perhaps close to the Orasje front-line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this BH Army of yours, what did that have to do with Orasje? There were the Croat forces there, the local Croats, organised to form Ustasha units. They did not recognise any BH officer as their own commanding officer; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's try to explain this. Orasje is close to the Sava River. The BH Army and the Croatian Defence Council, the 108, they were on the other side looking from the direction of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but my information suggests that it was along the Orasje front that Smail Camdzic as arrested, as well as Amir Durakovic, Jusuf Verise [phoen], and Major Seifudin Guric [phoen], who was the Chief of Staff of the 3rd Semberija Brigade, so there were these four Muslims who were with the Serb army. They were captured and later exchanged and released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, but I'll try to point this out again. They were captured by the BH Army or the HVO, the 108, not Orasje. What are you suggesting?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to my information, this was along the Orasje front-line, and the front-line ranged along this axis: Orasje, Krepcici, Markovici, Vasovic Polje, Vuksic. Is that right? Was that the line, the front-line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably was, but what I'm telling you, there was something going on on the other side of that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Semberija Brigade was a well respected Muslim called Pasaga Halilovic. He was the manager of the Duvan company, and I believe he still is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm really sorry to interrupt you, but I'm simply losing track of the direction here. Where are we going with all of this? Can you clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harhoff, I'll only be too happy to clarify. In Bijeljina, there were clashes between the Serb forces and the Muslim forces as a matter of principle. However, the actual clashes erupted between the forces who wanted to preserve Yugoslavia on the one hand and the ones who were in favour of an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina on the other. A considerable number of Muslims were in favour of preserving Yugoslavia. They fought for the Serb Army, on the side of the Serb Army, and this wasn't just Bijeljina. It was in other towns, too, there. My information suggests something about Bosanska Posavina as well. There was a Muslim unit within the Serb Army, and its name was - a detachment - Mesa Selimovic Detachment. For example, there were a number of other situations like that. The objective was not to wipe out the Muslims. The objective was to keep Bosnia and Herzegovina within Yugoslavia. It wasn't about any intolerance that the Serbs might have harboured for the Muslims. That's not what it was about. The crimes against the Muslims, the looting and expulsions occurred later on, sometime later once Mauzer had taken control of Bijeljina. Why? The Serb authorities were renaming streets across town after well-known Muslims, Camil Sijaric, for example. Vati Salamumba [phoen], there was a street that was called that. He was a politician from Congo. He was a national fighter during the non-aligned movement, and then it occurred to someone to name a street in Bijeljina after him. So the Serb authorities thought it was appropriate that that street should be renamed after the great fighter who was a Muslim -- a Serb writer who was a Muslim, Camil Sijaric. I think that's highly relevant. Let me draw your attention to everything that is there in the platform of the Serb Radical Party and the Serb Chetnik Movement. Before that, we were in favour of the brotherhood and unity of Serb -- Orthodox Serbs, Muslim Serbs, Catholic Serbs, Protestant Serbs, all united. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But the difficulty I have is that as noble as the motives behind all of this may ever be, what this trial is concerned with are the crimes that were committed in the wake of the attempts to keep the Greater Yugoslavia or Yugoslavia together.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Mr. Harhoff, but one must also establish who was really responsible for those crimes, who was out to commit those crimes, what were their motives, and what actions exactly led to those crimes or contributed to the commission of those crimes. It's not simply about the desire to preserve Yugoslavia at the cost of armed combat. That in itself is not a crime. Nevertheless, there were many shady dealings that became part of all the fighting that erupted later on. So what shady dealings are we talking about exactly? What I'm telling you is that those who were in favour of preserving Yugoslav what were not by their nature criminals. Well, now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think we've been through this many times before. The issue of the armed conflict, as such, is not at stake in this trial. It's only the crimes that were committed during the armed conflict, and this is what you're up against.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether you have already found evidence that a crime can be attached to me or linked to me. I haven't seen it anywhere. Maybe you have. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm completely neutral in this. I'm just telling you that you're accused -- you're up against the indictment that charges you for responsibility for some of these crimes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us now look at document 1525, if we may have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You read out a part of that document which the Prosecutor asked you to read. You have seen that the Serbian Volunteer Guards are mentioned here explicitly as a paramilitary formation linked to various criminal activities; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Nowhere in that document is there mention of the Serbian Radical Party. However, in para 8 on page 4 of that document -- do we have it now before us? Page 4, please, paragraph 8. It says: "By effective preventive measures, attempts at armed conflict were prevented by large groups of people belonging to various paramilitary formations." And then there is mention of the Red Berets, Captain Dragan's groups and so on, of course, local groups which essentially were prompted by motives of plunder and not ideological aims as they tried to portray themselves. Are they right in saying this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Red Berets belonged to Captain Dragan, and they were formed already in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, now you see on page 5 of this document, we see on the first page that this document is addressed to Dr. Radovan Karadzic, President of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On the last page, page 5, it now says in Radovan Karadzic's handwriting: "Continue with the enforcing of law and order. August the 2nd, 1992, Radovan Karadzic." Can you see this handwritten note?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it follows from this - this is an authentic document - that Radovan Karadzic advised law and order to be re-established in the area of Bijeljina. Do you know that for months after the liberation of Bijeljina - I'm calling it the liberation, you can call it capture, whatever you like - there were individual and group expulsions of the Muslim population from Bijeljina; their property was looted, they were expelled, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, already at the beginning of July some persons were expelled from their homes. If you had two houses, you had to empty one of them, and other persons of other ethnicity would move in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know who did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you heard of someone who called himself Major Vojkan Djurkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The press wrote about him too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he participated in these evictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you believe that he was a major of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that rank came from before the war, but he was never a military man, and it's not easy to get such a rank, even if he had been in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he was a self-proclaimed major belonging to Arkan's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, because as I was saying, he was not a member of the regular army before that, and later on if he attributed this rank to himself, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, if you left Bijeljina in 1992, had you ever heard that Mirko Blagojevic, heading the Serbian Radical Party, and our party in Bijeljina were constantly opposing Mauzer's arbitrariness and the persecution and eviction of any Muslims from Bijeljina? The Hague Prosecution has written declarations signed by Mirko Blagojevic opposing the eviction of Muslims. Did you hear of this, as a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear about it, but I do know that there were major conflicts between not individuals but groups in Bijeljina. There were disagreements, and the situation was aggravated by these persons, by Blagojevic's group, Mauzer's group, and very frequently there were clashes between them, even armed clashes. Why, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the Serbian authorities in Pale, the authority of Radovan Karadzic and the Serbian Democratic Party, never managed to neutral Mauzer, though they wanted to do that and they tried to do it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that Mauzer became a member of Zoran Djindjic's Democratic Party and the vice-President of that party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must have been later, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that after the Dayton Agreement, Ljubisa Savic, Mauzer, as President of Djindjic's Party for Republika Srpska participated in the elections?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, but in those days I had no contacts. I was not aware of any parties, who belonged to who and what they were doing, so I can't say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. We'll leave the parties aside. Do you know that when Biljana Plavsic carried out a coup in Republika Srpska and formed a government, that under the influence of foreigners, Ljubisa Savic, Mauzer, was appointed deputy minister of the interior and the head of the police for Republika Srpska? Did you hear of that? You should have heard that Mauzer had that position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear that, but I can't be specific. For the whole period after Dayton, I think he was killed. I'm not sure. As I was saying, what he was, where he was, where they were, I can't say. I wasn't au courant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. We won't go into who killed him, though there are certain clues there too. But is it clear to you now as a Muslim who lived in Bijeljina who lived with the Serbs and who had good and bad experiences with the Serbs, depending on the kind of persons they were, but as a Muslim who had relations with their policemen, that someone like Mauzer through expulsions of Muslims was intentionally doing a service to Serb -- to these opponents of Serbs if the authority in Pale was never able to settle accounts with Mauzer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that because I really don't know whether Mauzer was under the control of Mr. Karadzic or someone else. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. I assume that during the war or after the war, you must have been in Tuzla, and you had occasion to talk to your compatriots there. Did you hear from Serbs who had fled Bijeljina all the things that Mauzer did to the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear so much about Mr. Mauzer, but regarding the expulsions, I did hear who did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard of Djurkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Vojkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that Blagojevic or someone from the Radical Party took part in the persecution and eviction of Muslims from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did you hear of them publicly standing in the defence of the Muslims? Recently, a book was published in Tuzla who expressed gratitude for this defence of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we slow down a little bit because --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm in a hurry because I have little time left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope I'll manage to cover the most important points.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was reference to the destruction of a mosque. You yourself said that mosques were destroyed a certain time after the conflict; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a couple of months later; not all at once, but in a period between the autumn of 1992 and the spring of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the main mosques were killed about a year after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a whole year, but five or six months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you have any information as to who exactly stands behind the destruction of the mosques in Bijeljina and the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that Mirko Blagojevic and the Serbian Radical Party in Bijeljina opposed this fiercely and publicly condemned all such moves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see. You don't know that either. You said here - and I must say this surprised me a little bit, I must admit - you spoke about a man, saying of him that he had given instructions to collect the bodies after the conflict; is that so? And that man, according to your statement here, was called Seval Begic. You said about him that he had headed the utilities company in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I said that he organised the car for the transport of the dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here is what you say in your last statement, and it coincides with other statements. It's in paragraph 16: "The mortuary van was the property of the service headed by Seval Begic. He came to the police station and took us to two employees who were instructed to collect the bodies in town, and though I cannot remember their names, I know that they were full-time employees of the utilities company." That is what you say in your statement. Now, what I am confused by is in another place in the same statement, you say that the Serbian police wanted to arrest Seval Begic as a member of the Presidency of the SDA, that is, the Muslim Party of Democratic Action, but he had already left the area because he knew that he was being searched for by the Serbs. How can you explain this contradiction? Is it a contradiction because there was manipulation by the Prosecution with the text of your statement, or did you make such a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that the police did not arrest anyone at that time, and I -- this may be a mistake in the statement, but he was looked for by the people from the Crisis Staff and not by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who was looking for him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff of Bijeljina Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but on the one hand he's almost giving instructions to the police, he's coming to fetch you, he's giving orders. You said, We were under the control of Seval Begic, and he gave us orders. You said that in your first statement; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, we'll find it in your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never under the control of Seval Begic. Well, let's see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, in the statement, Witness, it is stated that upon arriving at the police station, two employees -- he took two employees and instructed them to go and collect bodies in the city, so these were police employees, were they? These were police employees, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were employees of the public utilities enterprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I had a doubt. Thank you for elucidating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was Seval Begic the manager of that company at all? Was he the director of this communal enterprise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, whether he was a director of that company or a branch of that company, but as far as I know, he worked there. Now, whether he was a supervisor or something, but the organisation went through him, the organisation of providing the vehicle and the personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, a Serb, Milan Peric, was the manager of the communal enterprise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the communal enterprise, but then the public utilities included water, heating, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. But Seval Begic, according to my information, was a teacher and he worked as an engineer in the Mladost pipe factory which was called Teleflex. That is where he was employed. He was no manager in the public utilities company, nor did he work there. I find this a little strange.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Seval Begic personally. But after those events, actually, that is when I met him. I may have made a mistake. I may have thought that he was a manager. But I repeat once again, this person was the contact person between the police and the organisation of the vehicle for the transportation of bodies and the personnel engaged to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, your time is up. Prosecutor, in a little time, do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I have only one issue I want to discuss with the witness, and I can inform you that we are now able to play you the video where Mr. -- Ms. Biljana Plavsic arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How long does it last?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I did not have a chance to see it, but it will not last -- less than a minute, I guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The stills I showed before are from this video. Can I move it into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We shall give the video a number now. Since we already had the stills, let's now give the video a number as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video will be Exhibit P745.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I want to ask or to know from you if you remember that Mirko Blagojevic was searched by the police in the time-period of 1990.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what you mean. You mean were the police looking for him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I mean if the police was looking for him for crimes committed not in the former Yugoslavia but in other European countries.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Blagojevic has been convicted for crimes in other European countries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-1035 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would finish my redirect. I did not discuss it with the witness before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, thank you very much for having come at the request of the OTP to testify on the events that took place at Bijeljina and in the surrounding area. Thank you for having answered all the questions raised by the Judges, Mr. Seselj, as well as the OTP. My best wishes to you for your return journey to your country. Before the hearing ends, as I already said, the next witness will be heard as long as his health permits it at the hearing that begins at quarter past 2.00 on Tuesday. Is that there anything new, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The witness that was scheduled to appear today, VS-1010, has now been rescheduled until the 11th of February. The witness that was listed for next week, Witness VS-1066, will appear Tuesday and Wednesday of next week as scheduled. So today's witness will move down the road a week. I will indicate so that there is no problems next week, Witness 1066, who's scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday, is scheduled to appear in another country in legal proceedings on Friday, so it would be absolutely important for us to get him done by the close of the court session on Wednesday so that he can travel to another country to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem. I don't have the file right here, but how much had you asked for 1066?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [In English] Two hours, yes. [Interpretation] So Mr. Seselj will have two hours. We will indeed need two days. That's no problem. Very well. Thank you. Thank you to everyone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What shall we do on day 3 next week? We have a total of three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The witness scheduled for next Thursday remains on the schedule, VS-1104. So the order will be -- next week we will have 1066 on Tuesday and Wednesday, 1104 on Thursday. The following week, we only sit Wednesday and Thursday because of the other trial. We will have Witness 1010 on 11 February and, if possible, Witness 1029 on the 12th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So everybody is fully informed of how things will proceed. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say that I've been sufficiently informed. I want this in writing today, if possible, because I don't think I've been able to memorise the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall send you an e-mail to confirm this, but in any case, next week -- generally, you have very quick thought processes, but perhaps I'm mistaken. Next week, 1066 will testify over two days, Tuesday and Wednesday, and then he has to leave because he has other obligations, and on Thursday we will hear 1104. Is that all right now? Fine. Good. Have a nice afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of February, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.16 p.m.,
